sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in San Marcos?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer, and in San Marcos the best fit depends mostly on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close. A college town on the Interstate 35 corridor between Austin and San Antonio has steady buyer traffic, but a home that needs work or carries an unpaid tax bill can still sit.

San Marcos is the Hays County seat, about 25 miles south of Austin on I-35, according to the Texas State Historical Association. The city also reaches into Guadalupe County, which matters because two different appraisal districts may handle parcels here. Check which district covers your lot before you read a tax statement.

A cash sale trims the steps that slow a listing: showings, buyer financing, lender appraisals and repair negotiations. The trade is a price below what a fully repaired, well staged listing might bring. Ask for a written offer, read what it says about repairs and closing costs, and compare it with what an agent would net after commission.

sections.h2: What does the San Marcos housing market look like?
sections.html:
San Marcos is a renter-heavy city. The Census Bureau lists the owner-occupied rate at 30.8 percent for 2020 to 2024 and the median value of owner-occupied homes at $310,400.

Those figures sit beside a few others that shape how a seller should think about buyers:

  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 77,830, up 14.9 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.
  • Households in 2020 to 2024: 28,013, with 2.28 persons per household.
  • Median gross rent: $1,322 a month.
  • Median selected monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $1,899; without a mortgage: $706.
  • Land area: 35.59 square miles, or 1,898 people per square mile in 2020.

With so many renters, investors who buy houses to rent out are a large part of the demand for older or rough homes. That helps a seller whose house needs a new roof or foundation work, since those buyers expect to price the repairs in.

sections.h2: How did San Marcos grow, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The town grew around the San Marcos Springs and the river, and the Texas Handbook traces its commercial life to the arrival of the International-Great Northern Railroad on August 31, 1880. Education became a local industry after the state chartered a normal school in 1899, and that school opened in 1903 as Southwest Texas State Normal School, the school that later grew into Southwest Texas State University.

The Handbook says education became the single largest employer in the city during the 1960s, and that Hays County joined the Austin metropolitan area in 1973. It also notes that by the mid 1980s at least 20 percent of the county labor force worked in Travis County.

For a seller, this means demand follows the academic calendar and Austin commuting patterns. Houses near campus and houses near the highway attract different buyers, so ask for offers that explain how the price was set.

sections.h2: Which San Marcos schools and rules affect your sale?
sections.html:
San Marcos ISD is one of the school districts the Guadalupe Appraisal District lists among the units it appraises for. Buyers with children usually ask which district a house sits in, so have that answer ready.

The city also regulates rentals. San Marcos Code Compliance states that owners of short term and long term rentals inside the city must register the property under city ordinances, and its officers patrol more than 30 square miles. If you are selling a rental, the registration status is worth confirming with the city before you set a closing date, because a buyer or title company may ask for it. Report or ask about code issues through the Code Compliance line at 512-393-8479.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and exemptions work when you sell in San Marcos?
sections.html:
Hays County parcels are appraised by the Hays Central Appraisal District, which does not send bills or take payments. The Hays County Tax Office handles bills and payments, and the tax office says it has no say over appraised values or exemptions.

Texas has no state property tax, so every figure comes from local taxing units. The tax lien attaches on January 1 and the owner on that date is liable for the year, which is why the proration at closing matters.

Texas property tax dates that apply to a San Marcos house (Texas Comptroller)
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set and the tax lien attaches
April 1 or soon afterAppraisal notices go out for homesteads
May 15Usual protest deadline with the review board, or 30 days after notice if later
October 1Tax bills are mailed
January 31Last day to pay without penalty; February 1 is delinquent

Schools must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, and owners 65 or older or disabled get another $60,000 school exemption, per the Comptroller. Hays CAD also audits every granted homestead once every five years, so a seller who moved out should not leave the exemption running.

sections.h2: What does the closing and recording process involve?
sections.html:
A deed for a San Marcos house is recorded with the county clerk of the county where the land sits, and it must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or similar officer. The state court manual lists a first page fee of $5.00 and $4.00 for each added page, plus smaller clerk fees.

If the house came through an inheritance, the paperwork differs by route:

  • Will probated: an executor's deed, or a court order with the will if the muniment route was used.
  • No will and a small estate: the Texas small estate affidavit covers estates of $75,000 or less, excluding the homestead, and homestead copies are recorded with the clerk.
  • Transfer on death deed: an affidavit of death and the death certificate, recorded with the county clerk.

Ask your title company which route applies before you accept an offer, because the wrong paperwork can add weeks.

sections.h2: What if the house is in foreclosure, has tenants, or needs repairs?
sections.html:
Each of those problems has a calendar, and a cash buyer can often work inside it. For a Texas foreclosure, the servicer must send a notice of sale at least 21 days before an auction held on the first Tuesday of the month, and a borrower can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice.

For tenants, a landlord needs a written notice to vacate, normally three days unless the lease says otherwise, then a justice court suit. A writ of possession can issue six days after judgment. Selling with a tenant in place is also an option when the buyer wants the lease.

Repairs are the easiest case. A buyer who purchases as is takes on the roof, plumbing and cosmetic work, so you skip contractor bids and the buyer's inspection requests.

faqs.q: Can I sell my San Marcos house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer or investor can purchase the house as is, and you decide whether the net offer beats a repaired listing. Compare a written offer against an agent's estimate of net proceeds after commission and repairs.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a San Marcos home?
faqs.a: The tax office of the county where the parcel sits sends it. In Hays County that is the Hays County Tax Office, and the Hays Central Appraisal District only sets values and exemptions. Bills go out around October 1 and are delinquent after January 31.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a San Marcos rental before selling it?
faqs.a: San Marcos Code Compliance says owners of short term and long term rentals must register under city ordinances. Confirm your registration status with the city, since a buyer or title company may ask about it.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in San Marcos?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on title work and the buyer, so ask for a closing date in writing. Probate, liens or unpaid taxes can add time, and a clear title usually moves the fastest.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption end when I sell?
faqs.a: A buyer who takes the house after January 1 can apply for the exemption for the rest of that tax year if the prior owner did not receive it, per the Comptroller. Tell the Hays Central Appraisal District that you moved out so its records stay accurate.
